passage: I'm Vidya, and for my first year I said yes to everything. When Raghav, my manager, forwarded a client report at 9 pm and wanted it by morning, I did it, resented him quietly, and got short with everyone. One Sunday he asked me to update the website banners, which isn't my role, and I nearly said "fine" again. Instead I said, "I can't take that on; I'm on the accounts. If it matters, who decides whether the banners or the accounts come first?" He looked surprised, then said the marketing lead decides. I also offered to send after-hours tasks a note by 5 pm so he could plan. It felt shaky at the time, but the resentment eased a lot.

qa.q: Whom did Raghav say decides whether the banners or the accounts come first?
qa.a: Raghav said the marketing lead decides.

qa.q: How did Vidya feel about Raghav's 9 pm requests in the first year?
qa.a: Vidya resented them quietly, which showed in getting short with everyone. Vidya may also have been afraid to say no.

qa.q: What made Vidya's refusal about the banners work better than the earlier silence?
qa.a: Vidya stated a limit, asked who decides and offered an alternative, instead of agreeing and resenting it.

qa.q: How might Raghav have seen Vidya's earlier yeses?
qa.a: He may have assumed the late work was fine with Vidya, since Vidya never said otherwise.

grounding: A young professional sets limits on after-hours work, declines a task outside their role and asks who authorises decisions, offering an alternative.

passage: Supervisor's note, Harish, logistics desk. This week the night lead asked Ojas to cover a weekend shift that was not on his roster and also to sign off a vendor change. Ojas told the lead, "I can't do the weekend; I have family commitments. I can take the Friday evening handover instead." On the sign-off he said, "That is above my role. Who authorises it?" The lead looked irritated and said nothing for a while. Ojas kept his tone even, though he looked tired and rubbed his neck. I stepped in and named the regional manager as the approver. I have asked both of them to write down after-hours cover rules for the team.

qa.q: What alternative did Ojas offer for the weekend shift?
qa.a: He offered to take the Friday evening handover instead.

qa.q: What might Ojas have been feeling as he rubbed his neck?
qa.a: He probably felt tired and tense after saying no to the lead, although the gesture alone could just be plain tiredness.

qa.q: What did Harish do that helped settle the sign-off question?
qa.a: Harish named the regional manager as the approver, and asked both people to write down after-hours cover rules.

qa.q: How might the night lead have felt about Ojas's answers?
qa.a: The lead looked irritated and went quiet, maybe from worry about cover or from feeling questioned; the note does not say which.

grounding: A young professional refuses an out-of-role task, limits weekend work with an alternative and asks who authorises a decision, seen by a supervisor.

passage:
Thursday, 10:30 pm
Kunal messaged again at 10:15. "Quick one, can you check the numbers on slide 12?" Third night this week. Every time, I've just done it, fuming, typing with my jaw tight, then lying awake annoyed at him and more annoyed at myself.
Today I finally said something. Not in a snap, which is what I'd been rehearsing in the shower. I went to his desk at lunch and said, "Kunal, I'm not able to work after nine on weekdays. If something's urgent, message me before six and I'll prioritise it, or tell me first thing and I'll do it by ten." He looked surprised. "Oh. Sorry, I didn't realise. I just send things when I think of them."
So tonight I didn't answer. Phone face down.
Tomorrow at 9:30 I'll check slide 12.
Sunaina

qa.q: When did Kunal's latest message arrive?
How had Sunaina been feeling about the late messages?
qa.a: Sunaina had been resentful and annoyed, fuming while doing the work and lying awake angry at Kunal and at herself.

qa.q: What made Sunaina's limit effective?
qa.a: It was stated calmly in person, not in a snap, and came with alternatives: messages before six, or first thing for a fix by ten.

qa.q: How did Kunal react to the limit?
qa.a: Kunal was surprised and apologetic, explaining he just sent things when he thought of them, not expecting instant replies.

grounding: Shows a young professional moving from silent resentment to stating an after-hours limit with alternatives.

passage:
Tanvir: hey, can you approve the Sharma Traders invoice? it's stuck and they keep calling me
Devika: I can't approve invoices, that's outside my role. only the finance leads can
Tanvir: yeah but you have access to the system. just click it
Devika: I have view access, not approval. and even if I could, it wouldn't be right without Meera signing off
Tanvir: ugh. they'll shout at me again 😩
Devika: I get it. two options: I message Meera now and flag it as urgent, or you forward me the invoice and I put it at the top of tomorrow's finance queue
Tanvir: message Meera. please
Devika: done. she says she'll approve it by 4
Tanvir: ok that's actually better than me begging you. thanks
Devika: 👍 anytime you need to know who signs what, ask me

qa.q: Who can approve invoices?
qa.a: Only the finance leads.

qa.q: How was Tanvir feeling about the stuck invoice?
qa.a: Tanvir felt stressed and anxious, dreading being shouted at again by the vendor.

qa.q: How did Devika refuse the task well?
qa.a: Devika explained it was outside the role and who authorises it, then offered two alternatives and quickly got Meera to approve by four.

qa.q: What would have happened if Devika had simply clicked approve?
qa.a: Meera's sign-off would have been bypassed, possibly causing trouble for both of them, even if Tanvir felt relieved for a moment.

grounding: Shows a young professional refusing a task outside the role, naming who authorises it and offering alternatives.

passage: For the third Sunday in a row, Farhan, the panchayat secretary, knocked at Rehana's door in the village near Barabanki with a stack of forms. "Madam, just fill these household surveys. You're educated, it's quick." Rehana had done the first two stacks silently, resenting every page while her own lesson plans waited. This time she didn't take the forms. "Farhan-ji, I want to help, but this isn't part of my teaching duty. Who has authorised teachers to do this survey?" Farhan scratched his head. "The block office wants it done." "Then could you ask the block office to send an order in writing? If they assign it officially, I'll do my share on a weekday after school. And the anganwadi helper was trained for these surveys; she could take half." Farhan looked at the stack, then nodded. "I'll ask the block office tomorrow." Rehana closed the door and opened her lesson plans.

qa.q: How many Sundays in a row had Farhan brought forms?
qa.a: Three Sundays in a row.

qa.q: How had Rehana felt doing the first two stacks?
qa.a: Rehana felt resentful, doing the forms silently while her own lesson plans waited.

qa.q: How did Rehana set her limit effectively?
qa.a: She said calmly it wasn't her duty, asked who had authorised it, requested a written order, and offered alternatives: a weekday share and the anganwadi helper.

qa.q: How might Farhan have felt when Rehana asked who had authorised the survey?
qa.a: Farhan was probably a little caught out and uncertain, realising he needed the block office's order rather than her goodwill.

grounding: Shows a young professional moving from silent resentment to refusing out-of-role weekend work, asking who authorises it and offering alternatives.

passage:
At 10:40 on a Tuesday night, Soo-ah's phone buzzed on the kitchen counter of her Toronto apartment. Bilal again: "Can you redo the supplier contract tonight? Legal wants changes."
She stared at it. It was the third late message that week, and contracts weren't even her job; she handled scheduling. Last month she'd have said yes and then snapped at him in the morning.
She typed, deleted, typed again. "Hi Bilal, I'm offline for the night now. I can look first thing tomorrow, 9 am. Contract wording is outside my role, though; who in legal signs off on this? I can send them the schedule details they need."
Her heart thumped as she hit send.
At 8:55 the next morning Bilal replied: "Fair. I'll loop in Marta from legal. Can you send her the delivery dates by noon?"
"Yes," Soo-ah wrote, and meant it.

qa.q: What does Soo-ah handle at work?
qa.a: She handled scheduling.

qa.q: How did Soo-ah feel as she hit send?
qa.a: Soo-ah felt nervous, heart thumping, worried how Bilal would take the limit, but also determined not to end up resentful again.

qa.q: What made Soo-ah's message effective?
qa.a: It set the limit, gave a clear time she would be available, named what was outside her role, asked who signs off, and offered something useful instead.

qa.q: How did Bilal respond to the boundary?
qa.a: Bilal accepted it as fair, brought in Marta from legal and asked only for the delivery dates by noon.

grounding: A young professional sets a limit on late-night work and a task outside her role, asks who authorises it and offers an alternative instead of silent resentment.
